source.title: Warhammer 40,000: The App 2.7.1, data build 972, released 2026-10-02

data.summary:
The opposing player resolves each **save roll** in turn, lowest result first, until every attack is resolved or the whole target unit is **destroyed**; any attacks left over are then lost. For each roll:

1. Select Model: from the current allocation group, pick a wounded model if there is one.
2. Check Save Roll: the first matching case below applies.
3. Resolve Damage: on damage, the model loses wounds equal to the attack's D and is destroyed at 0 or fewer remaining wounds.

The save roll cases, in order:

- an unmodified 1 inflicts damage
- a roll at or above the group's InSv fails
- a roll at or above the model's Sv after applying the weapon's AP fails
- anything else inflicts damage

For example, AP -1 makes a 3 rolled to save into a 2, which fails against Sv 2+ or better.

The current group begins as the group declared first, and moves on to the next one once every model in it is destroyed. For modifying damage, see 02.02.01.

A model has suffered damage once an attack allocated to it reaches Resolve Damage, even if a rule then ignores or prevents the lost wounds.

Destroyed models and units:

- a unit is destroyed once all its models are
- a destroyed model's on-destruction rules resolve first, then it is removed; if it has such rules and an attack destroyed it, both wait, by default, until the attacking unit's attacks are resolved
- unless stated otherwise, destroyed models and units lose their abilities, and rules cannot select or target them
- an enemy counts as destroyed by you or your army only if an attack by one of your models or one of your player rules destroyed it

A model allowed to attack after being destroyed stays in play until its unit has made its attacks after being **selected to attack**, or the phase ends, whichever is first; then its destruction rules resolve and it is removed. If it must fight right after the attacking unit, it instead stays until its own unit has fought or the phase ends, so the unit fights together and Stratagems used on the unit also affect it.

To measure to a destroyed model, use any point its base covered, or any part of the model if it is a **VEHICLE** or has no base (a **WALKER** with a base uses the base); to a destroyed unit, measure to its last destroyed model.

Worked examples cover boltguns, bolt pistols and a heavy bolter (BS 3+ and 4+, wounding T 3 on 3+) against Sv 3+ and InSv 5+, and an attached Saint Celestine unit whose **CHARACTER** group goes last.
